thread:
Maria Chen: Quick flag — during today’s Dedicated perf sweep I observed steady KV cache inflation on Dedicated nodes after ~2h of long-context streaming. Hosted runs of the same workload show a much flatter curve. Anyone else seeing this?
Zhou Li: I saw a related pattern in a Private VPC run earlier this week. Growth looks environment-dependent. Do you have numbers?
Maria Chen: On A100 Dedicated (baseline config: batch_window=12ms, continuous batching ON) — after ~2 hours RSS +1.2GB on the runtime process, KV slot usage up ~18% which pushes us into more frequent paging/eviction. Hosted same workload: only +200MB.
Taylor Ng: Did you capture kernel selection logs? Hosted sometimes picks fused attention kernels and that avoids an extra temp buffer path. That could explain the delta.
Maria Chen: Here's a short kernel log line I grabbed: 
```
kernel_choice=matmul_fused_v2 fallback=attn_unfused reason=seq>2048 batch=8
kv_reclaim_policy=lazy_coalesce
```
Zhou Li: That fallback path will allocate transient per-token buffers which interact badly with jemalloc slab fragmentation over long runs. We should check jemalloc stats.
Priyanka Rao: Also remember VPC networking constraints can change batching behavior — when packets are delayed (MTU/cwnd quirks) the batching window can stretch and accidentally increase concurrent KV footprint. Worth validating network perf in the VPC vs hosted region.
infra-bot: ci/perf-dedicated/kv-growth-run-1715554321 completed. Artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/kv/1715554321 (profiles + flamegraphs).
Maria Chen: Repro script I'm using: `scripts/repro/kv_longctx.sh --model tiny --seq 4096 --batch 8 --duration 7200` — please run on Hosted, Dedicated, and Private and paste `pmap` + `je_stats` for the runtime process.
Taylor Ng: Ran it on Hosted this afternoon. Kernel log shows `kernel_choice=attn_fused_v1` and `kv_reclaim=coalesce` consistently — explains lower fragmentation & lower RSS slope.
Priyanka Rao: Actionable checklist: 1) unify jemalloc config across Dedicated/Hosted (we currently have small alloc conf drift), 2) force the same kernel selection heuristics in a canary to see if that eliminates delta, 3) inspect on-prem driver stack (older drivers sometimes change page behavior).
Zhou Li: I'll dump `je_stats` + `mallctl` outputs from Dedicated and Private. If fragmentation metrics (active vs mapped) diverge, we can try increase background coalesce frequency.
DevEx: Suggest adding a short triage doc to docs.devx: "How to debug KV inflation" with repro commands and the key metrics to collect (pmap, je_stats, kernel_choice log, batching histograms).
Maria Chen: Assigning: @Zhou Li -> collect jemalloc and fragmentation metrics across clusters; @Priyanka Rao -> check kernel selection heuristics and quantized kernel fallbacks; @Taylor Ng -> run the repro on on-prem A100s and attach driver/kernel versions. I'll aggregate traces and upload a one-pager. Target: EOD sync.
Zhou Li: Ack, I'll include `malloc_conf` and `je-mib` dumps. If we confirm high fragmentation, we can test `malloc_conf:oversize_threshold` tuning or periodic `je_free` coalesce.
Priyanka Rao: Also watching for quantized code paths allocating extra host-side buffers — will flag any extra arena allocations.
Maria Chen: Thanks team. Labeling this thread `kv-inflation-investigation`. I'll post updates as we get runs.
